A2.text:
Tural sat in a small cafe in Icherisheher. He looked at his heavy books and sighed. He was only a first-year university student, but he already wanted to drop out.

His older sister Aysel walked into the cafe. She sat down across from him and smiled warmly.

“What is wrong, Tural?” she asked.

“My history exam is tomorrow. The deadline for my essay is also tomorrow,” he said. “I cannot do this. I want to leave university.”

Aysel shook her head. “No, you will not leave. We just need to hit the books together. I can help you.”

For three hours, Aysel helped him revise. She did not just read the textbook. She asked him questions. She wanted him to understand the story of the past.

“Do not just memorize,” she told him. “Think about the people.”

The next day, Tural took his exam. He felt nervous, but he remembered Aysel’s questions. He wrote his answers carefully.

A week later, Aysel called him. “How was the exam?” she asked.

“I got the highest mark in the class!” Tural laughed.

“See? You just needed a little help,” Aysel said.

“Yes,” Tural answered. “Now, can you help me every week?”

Aysel just laughed and hung up the phone.

questions.q: What is the story mainly about?
options: A student who gets a job in a cafe
A sister who wants to leave university
A boy who receives study help from his sister and does well
Two students who miss their history exam
questions.why: Tural wants to drop out, but Aysel helps him study and he gets the highest mark.

questions.q: What did Aysel tell Tural to do while studying?
questions.why: “Do not just memorize,” she told him. “Think about the people.”
Tural says, “I want to leave university,” and Aysel tells him, “No, you will not leave.”

questions.q: Aysel says they need to “hit the books”. What does this mean?
options: To return books to the library
questions.why: She says this right before they spend three hours revising for his exam.

questions.q: Why does Aysel laugh and hang up the phone at the end?
options: She is talking to someone else
She thinks his request for weekly help is funny
questions.why: Tural cheekily asks, “Now, can you help me every week?” and she laughs in response to his joke.

B1.text:
Tural sat in a quiet cafe near Ganjlik Mall, staring at a mountain of notes. He was in his first year of university, but he was already thinking about dropping out. The history curriculum was too difficult, and the deadline for his final essay was only two days away.

His older sister, Aysel, walked in and sat down with two cups of coffee. She studied at the same university and had a full scholarship.

“You look terrible,” Aysel laughed. “Are you ready for the exam?”

“Not at all,” Tural sighed. “I read the books, but I cannot remember dates and names. I think I need extra tuition.”

“You do not need to pay for a teacher. You just need to learn the ropes,” Aysel said warmly. “University is not about reading everything. It is about understanding the main ideas. Let’s hit the books together.”

For the next four hours, Aysel helped him revise. Instead of making him memorize facts, she taught him how to connect events. They talked about historical figures like real people. It felt less like a boring lesson and more like a great story.

On Friday, Tural walked into the exam hall. His heart was beating fast, but when he saw the questions, he smiled. They were exactly the kind of ideas he had discussed with Aysel.

Two weeks later, Tural met Aysel at the same cafe. He put a piece of paper on the table.

“Did you pass?” she asked, looking at his excited face.

“I didn’t just pass. I passed with flying colours!” Tural shouted happily. “I got an A.”

“That is amazing! I am very proud of you,” Aysel smiled.

“Thanks,” Tural said, sitting down. “So, what time does our next lesson start?”

questions.q: What is the main idea of the story?
options: University exams are impossible to pass without a private tutor
History is the most difficult subject at university
Learning how to study properly can help a student succeed
Brother and sister argue over their different study habits
questions.why: Aysel shows Tural how to study effectively instead of just memorizing, leading to his success.

questions.q: Why did Aysel not pay for her university studies?
questions.why: “She studied at the same university and had a full scholarship.”

questions.q: What did Tural find most difficult about his history course?
questions.why: “I read the books, but I cannot remember dates and names.”

questions.q: Tural took his history exam on Thursday.
questions.why: “On Friday, Tural walked into the exam hall.”

questions.q: Aysel says Tural just needs to “learn the ropes”. What does this phrase mean?
options: To learn how to do a specific task or job
questions.why: She means he needs to learn the right way to study at the university level.

questions.q: Why did Tural smile when he saw the exam questions?
options: He knew he could guess the answers
They were the exact topics he had studied with Aysel
He realized the exam was actually for a different subject
questions.why: “They were exactly the kind of ideas he had discussed with Aysel.”

B2.text:
Tural sat in a bustling cafe near the old walls of Icherisheher, staring blankly at a mountain of highlighted notes. It was only his first semester, but he was genuinely considering dropping out. The university's new history curriculum was far more demanding than he had expected, and the strict deadline for his final term paper was rapidly approaching.

His older sister, Aysel, suddenly appeared from the busy street outside and slid into the booth opposite him, placing two cappuccinos on the table. As a postgraduate student who had earned a prestigious academic scholarship, she knew exactly how to handle university pressure.

“You look like you haven't slept in a week,” she observed with a sympathetic smile.

“I haven't,” Tural groaned, rubbing his eyes. “I've been reading for days, but nothing stays in my head. I seriously think I might need private tuition to survive this course.”

“You don't need a tutor, you just need to learn the ropes of academic study,” Aysel replied smoothly. “At this level, basic historical literacy isn't enough. Professors aren't looking for a list of memorised dates; they want to see critical thinking. Come on, let's hit the books together.”

For the next four hours, Aysel guided him through a completely different way to revise. Instead of mindlessly repeating facts, she challenged him to analyse the causes and effects of historical events. They debated the motivations of political leaders, turning dry historical records into a fascinating puzzle.

By the time Friday morning's exam finally arrived, Tural's heavy anxiety had vanished. When he turned over the test paper, he didn't panic. He simply mapped out his arguments, just as they had practised.

A fortnight later, Tural found Aysel reading on a bench on the Boulevard. He silently handed her his results transcript.

Aysel scanned the page and grinned. “An A-minus! You didn't just survive, you passed with flying colours!”

“I couldn't have done it without your strategy,” Tural admitted, sitting beside her with a sigh of relief.

“Well, I'm always happy to help,” Aysel said, handing the paper back.

Tural smiled cheekily. “Excellent. Because my economics midterms are next month, and the syllabus looks terrifying.”

questions.q: What is the central theme of the text?
options: The importance of history in modern education
Mastering academic skills to overcome university challenges
How sibling rivalry affects university performance
The financial struggles of a first-year student
questions.why: The story focuses on Tural learning critical thinking and revision strategies from his sister to succeed in his demanding course.

questions.q: Why was Tural struggling with his course?
options: He had missed too many lectures
The new curriculum was very demanding
He had lost his academic scholarship
His professor gave him the wrong textbook
questions.why: “The university's new history curriculum was far more demanding than he had expected.”

questions.q: Where did Tural give Aysel his exam results?
options: In the bustling cafe near Icherisheher
On a bench on the Boulevard
questions.why: “Tural found Aysel reading on a bench on the Boulevard. He silently handed her his results transcript.”

questions.q: Aysel told Tural that university professors just want students to memorize facts and dates.
questions.why: “Professors aren't looking for a list of memorised dates; they want to see critical thinking.”

questions.q: Aysel says Tural “passed with flying colours”. What does this expression mean?
options: To finish an exam very quickly
To succeed very easily or with a high mark
To cheat on a test using colourful notes
questions.why: She says this excitedly after seeing he got an A-minus on his difficult exam.

questions.q: What can be inferred from Tural's final comment?
options: He plans to change his major to economics
He is going to drop out before the midterms
He is confident he can study economics without any help
He expects Aysel to tutor him for his economics exams too
questions.why: He cheekily says “Excellent. Because my economics midterms are next month,” implying he wants her to help him again.
